crime_highlights: He then started hitting the complainant’s head against the door.
He then dragged her to the living room and hit her head against the living room floor.
When she regained consciousness, the appellant’s hands were around her neck, and she could not breathe.
the appellant began hitting the complainant’s head against the driver’s side glass
The appellant told the complainant he would kill her if she told anyone what happened.
The complainant later attended the hospital and was treated for a concussion.
rationale_highlights: the trial judge stated that the appellant’s Indigenous identity did have an impact on his moral culpability
he considered the appellant’s Indigenous background to be the most significant mitigating factor in the case
I am of the view that as an Aboriginal person, your childhood has affected and has mitigated your moral culpability in this case.
The trial judge’s reasons make clear that he was alive to the Gladue report and the impact of the Gladue factors on the sentence.
taking into account both the aggravating features of these serious offences and the mitigating impact of the Gladue principles
note: Appeal court endorses trial judge's Gladue mitigation and applies it in resentencing.

crime_highlights: The appellant’s one-year old daughter nearly died after ingesting methamphetamines and fentanyl while in the appellant’s care in the family home.
rationale_highlights: The sentencing judge took into account other sentencing principles that mitigated the appellant’s moral culpability due to her difficult life circumstances
note: Brief oral reasons; Gladue report mentioned but no clear systemic mitigation stated.

crime_highlights: Mr. George was observed in a convenience store moving a firearm from his waistband to a bag he was carrying.
The gun he had put in the bag was loaded.
rationale_highlights: The mitigating circumstances included the anti-Black racism he had experienced
the trial judge found there was a link between the offences and the disadvantage described in the presentence report
The trial judge failed to explain why Mr. George’s flight should be treated as aggravating given the impact his experiences with the police could have had on that decision.
flight should not have been treated as an aggravating circumstance
note: Appeal court removes flight as aggravating given police experiences; reduces sentence.
